images.text:
NASA had to delay launching a space shuttle because of woodpeckers. Woodpeckers ... ? Like that little guy ... what's his name ... in the cartoon? That doesn't make any sense. You do agree ... I mean it does sound crazy ... right?

So, these woodpeckers ... yes, your garden variety woodpeckers ... punched dozens of holes in the foam insulation around the shuttle fuel tank as it sat on the launch pad.

Of course, the mission had to be put off. Workers were sent aloft in a 25-story crane to make repairs. The birds, it seems, had flown the coop ... so to speak. The wind did not cooperate. Consequently, they had to tow the fuel tank to the Vehicle Assembly Building ... about three miles away. This set back the launch ... wait for it ... a couple of months.

This is the first time that woodpeckers have caused such severe problems for the space shuttle program. Not that they would tell us anyway ... and why they would peck into the thick orange foam left NASA officials baffled.

Worse ... they are not sure what to do to protect future shuttles. NASA workers have tried to scare the woodpeckers off with plastic owls on the launch pad and loud noises, all to no avail. Have a good idea? I'm sure NASA would love to hear from you!

Intonation of Finished and Unfinished Ideas
When you speak English, it is up to you to make sure that you are clear when you speak.
The listener shouldn't have to work hard to understand the communication.
So when you speak, your voice should fully fall at the end of a thought group or sentence. This tells the person listening that you are finished with the statement.

On the other hand, your voice should partially fall at the end of a thought group to show that your are NOT finished with the statement.
This gives the listener time to think about what you have said and makes then expect you to continue.

Tonic, Contrastive, Emphatic and New Information Stress
There are various types of stress used when speaking English.
Tonic stress refers to the syllable in a word which receives the most stress in an intonation unit.

This is the first time
This is the first time / that woodpeckers
This is the first time that woodpeckers / have caused such severe problems for the space shuttle program.
When you want to point out the difference between one object and another, you use contrastive stress. It tends to be used with determiners such as 'this, that, these and those'.

For example:
Not this book, that one
To emphasize a word, you can change the stress from the principal word to another content word. By choosing a word other than the one you normally stress, you put emphasis on the new one.

For example:
This is not the right way!
Sentence stress gives English its rhythm or "beat".
When you stress new information, you pronounce new information with more breath force, since it is more prominent.
Example: NASA had to delay launching a space shuttle.
